bounded_pass: One constructive source/proof pass; no additional reviewer and no shared writer-owned edits.
finding: Two-embedded-sheet cleanliness does not imply avoidance of an entire immersed image. The original common ambient composition cannot cancel any double point, and all-times self-transversality is incompatible with cancellation. Framing scaffolds additionally confuse normal ranks and fixed versus adjustable boundary framing.

item.title: A collared Whitney disk can avoid an entire compact immersed image
item.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M^m$ be closed, $m\ge3$, let $X^{2m}$ be boundaryless, and let $f:M\looparrowright X$ be an immersion. Suppose a smooth disk map $H:D^2\to X$ is an embedding on a boundary collar and the interior of that collar is disjoint from $f(M)$. Then arbitrarily close to $H$ there is an embedded disk $W$ homotopic to $H$ relative to a smaller fixed boundary collar and satisfying $W(\operatorname{int}D^2)\cap f(M)=\varnothing$. If $H$ is already an embedding, $W$ can be chosen arbitrarily $C^1$-close through embedded disks, and any supplied framing that already extends over $H$ is transported with unchanged boundary values. For a Whitney boundary avoiding every other double point, the supporting tube can be chosen disjoint from neighbourhoods of those other double points and meeting the immersed image only in the designated source-sheet collars. This is an immersion-image adapter; it does not assert extension of an arbitrary prescribed boundary frame.
item.proof:
**Given:** Countable choice, a closed smooth $m$-manifold $M$, $m\ge3$, an immersion $f:M\to X^{2m}$, and a smooth disk map $H:D^2\to X$ whose restriction to an open boundary collar is an embedding and whose collar interior is disjoint from $f(M)$. Corners of a Whitney circle are treated with its fixed corner model, or rounded compatibly; all perturbations are away from the boundary.

1.1 Compactness makes $f$ proper and $f(M)$ closed. Cover $M$ by finitely many immersion charts $U_i$ on which $f$ is an embedding; use slightly smaller relatively compact charts covering $M$. Fix closed nested collars $C\subset\operatorname{int}_{D^2}C^+$ inside the given collar, and keep $H$ fixed on a neighbourhood of $C$. The transition annulus is compact, embedded, and disjoint from $f(M)$; its positive distance from this closed image and openness of embeddings on the larger compact collar let all sufficiently small perturbations preserve these properties on the protected collar. No positive distance is asserted on the whole open disk interior, which accumulates on its boundary in $f(M)$. [given, construct]

1.2 Make $H$ an immersion relative to the collar. Embed $X$ in Euclidean space and use its smooth neighbourhood retraction as in the published tubular-target perturbation supplier. On finitely many disk charts covering the compact unprotected core, choose smooth bumps supported off $C$, equal to one on smaller charts, and multiply these bumps by the constant and both coordinate functions. Give each of these three profiles independent ambient-vector parameters. Composing the resulting Euclidean perturbation with the target retraction gives a family whose 1-jet parameter differential spans independently the value and both derivative columns at each core point: constants vary the value, and a linear combination of constant and coordinate profiles vanishing at that point varies either derivative column without varying the value. Surjectivity holds at parameter zero and, by a finite compact cover, on a sufficiently small parameter ball. The rank-$r$ matrix stratum for maps $\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^{2m}$ has codimension $(2-r)(2m-r)$: on the chart where an $r\times r$ minor is invertible, the remaining Schur-complement block must vanish and gives exactly that many independent equations. Parametric transversality to the rank-0 and rank-1 strata therefore avoids both, because their codimensions exceed 2 (the least is $2m-1>2$). On the protected collar immersion persists by smallness. Choose a sufficiently small good parameter, obtaining an immersion $h$ fixed near $C$. This uses only finitely many profiles and the actual parametric-transversality theorem; no unproved relative jet theorem is invoked. [construct, algebra]

2.1 A compact immersion $h:D^2\to X$ has a uniform near-diagonal injectivity radius, stable under sufficiently small $C^1$ perturbations. To see the stability rather than merely assert it, cover $D^2$ by finitely many smaller disk charts in which a two-coordinate projection of a target chart composed with $h$ has derivative near a fixed invertible matrix. Shrink to convex charts. For all close maps the derivative of the projected map still differs from that matrix by less than its least singular value, so integration along the segment between two source points proves injectivity there. A Lebesgue radius for this finite cover excludes coincidences with $0<d(z,z')<\delta$. This argument applies in boundary charts too because the collar is fixed. Now use finitely many finer bump charts of diameter less than $\delta/3$, supported off $C$, with independent constant-vector parameters. They span value directions on the unprotected core. On the transition collar any unmoved pair is already distinct, and charts and parameter size can be chosen so that any possible separated coincidence involving that collar has at least one point in the fully adjustable core; compactness excludes the other pairs. For a pair at distance at least $\delta$ the parameters supported at its adjustable point move that image in all target directions while leaving the other point fixed. Thus the pair evaluation $(z,z',a)\mapsto(h_a(z),h_a(z'))$ is transverse to the target diagonal at every possible coincidence. Parametric transversality makes the separated coincidence preimage empty since its expected dimension is $4-2m<0$. Apply it on an open separated-pair region (or its boundary strata separately); the uniform near-diagonal estimate excludes all remaining pairs. The map is still an immersion by $C^1$ smallness and hence a compact injective immersion, so is an embedding $w_0$, fixed on the collar. [step 1.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 Finally perturb this embedded disk to avoid the entire immersed image. A sufficiently small $C^1$ perturbation of a compact embedding remains embedded, by the uniform local estimate and the positive separation of images of pairs outside a diagonal neighbourhood. Construct a finite value-spanning parameter family $w_a$ supported off the protected collar, using the same bump/retraction construction; on its compact transition annulus avoidance of $f(M)$ persists by smallness. For each immersion chart put $R_i=\{(f(y),y):y\in U_i\}\subset X\times U_i$. This is an embedded graph of codimension $2m$, even when different branches of $f(M)$ cross. On the adjustable disk region the map $(z,y,a)\mapsto(w_a(z),y)$ is transverse to $R_i$ because the parameter derivative spans $T_{w_a(z)}X$. On the protected collar interior and transition annulus there are no incidences at all. Relative parametric transversality, implemented by these vanishing profiles, gives parameters for which every slice is transverse to every $R_i$; the exceptional sets have finite null union, and good parameters exist arbitrarily near zero. The incidence preimage has dimension $2+m-2m=2-m<0$, hence is empty for $m\ge3$. The finite charts cover every source branch, so $w_a(\operatorname{int}D^2)\cap f(M)=\varnothing$, including all double-point branches. Boundary incidences are intentionally excluded from the domain of this transversality argument. Set $W=w_a$ at one such small parameter. [step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Straight parameter segments in the retraction families give smooth homotopies relative to the fixed collar. The disk can be chosen arbitrarily close to $H$; when $H$ was already an embedded disk, steps 1.2 and 2.1 are unnecessary and step 3.1 alone gives arbitrarily $C^1$-small perturbations through embedded disks. A supplied actual normal framing of that embedded disk is transported along this small embedding isotopy by its normal-bundle isomorphisms, chosen to be the identity on the fixed collar. Thus any supplied boundary framing that already extended remains unchanged there and still extends; no assertion is made that an arbitrary prescribed boundary framing extends initially. The finitely many other double points lie outside $W$, including its boundary by hypothesis, so compactness permits a disk tube disjoint from neighbourhoods of them. Near its boundary the tube meets $f(M)$ only in the designated source-sheet collars: compactness of the complement of those source collars excludes stray branches, while the local immersion charts give the designated sheets. This is the required cleanliness relative to the entire image. [step 3.1, construct] ∎

item.title: A normal summand of rank at least two realizes every framing-loop obstruction
item.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For N > r >= 2, the standard block inclusion SO(r) into SO(N) is surjective on fundamental groups. Hence a loop discrepancy of a total normal frame can be killed by a loop supported in a single rank-r orthogonal summand, leaving its subspace and designated corner values fixed.
item.proof:
**Given:** Integers $N>r\ge2$ and the standard block inclusion $SO(r)\subset SO(N)$.

1.1 The map $SO(N)\to V_{N-r}(\mathbb R^N)$ taking the first $N-r$ columns has fibre $SO(r)$. Gram–Schmidt completion gives local continuous sections: near a fixed frame project a fixed complementary basis orthogonally off that frame, orthonormalize, and choose the last sign to make determinant positive. These sections give local trivializations, and a partition of unity on the compact Stiefel base makes the bundle numerable, hence a fibration. [given, construct]

1.2 The Stiefel-connectivity supplier gives $\pi_1(V_{N-r}(\mathbb R^N))=0$ since $N\ge(N-r)+2$. The fibration long exact sequence therefore makes $\pi_1(SO(r))\to\pi_1(SO(N))$ surjective. For a boundary normal frame $F$ compared with a global disk normal frame, the difference is a loop in $SO(N)$ (after matching orientation); choose a loop in $SO(r)$ representing its inverse class, apply it within that normal summand, and the corrected total loop is nullhomotopic and extends over $D^2$. A based loop can be reparametrized to be constant outside the interior of one chosen boundary arc, so all corner frames and the splitting subspaces are unchanged. This proves correction of a freely chosen admissible frame, not extension of every previously prescribed frame. [step 1.1, construct] ∎

consumer_patch.replace_statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a closed connected $m$-manifold with $m\ge3$, let $X$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $2m$, and let $f:M^m\looparrowright X$ be a self-transverse immersion.

1. Let $r_1\neq r_2$ be double points of $f$, equipped with a choice of branches and with arcs $\alpha$ in one branch and $\beta$ in the other joining them and avoiding all other double-point preimages, such that the resulting Whitney circle $\gamma=\alpha*\beta$ is null-homotopic in $X$ (automatic when $X$ is simply connected, and in general equivalent to equality of the two fundamental-group labels). Suppose the two double points have opposite local signs with respect to the chosen branch pairing; when $m$ is even this is a genuine condition on the ordered branch pair, and when $m$ is odd the ordering of the two branches may be chosen at one of the two points so that the signs are opposite. Then there is a smooth regular homotopy $f_t$, $t\in[0,1]$, through immersions $M\to X$, with $f_0=f$ and $f_1$ self-transverse which is constant outside a compact neighbourhood of a clean Whitney disk for $\gamma$ and near every double point other than $r_1,r_2$, and such that $\Sigma(f_1)=\Sigma(f)\setminus\{r_1,r_2\}$: the pair is removed and no new double point appears. Intermediate maps remain immersions; the cancellation can pass through a branch tangency, so self-transversality is required at the endpoints. The family is a regular homotopy ([[def-regular-homotopy-of-immersions]]).

2. If the double points of $f$ can be partitioned into finitely many pairs admissible as in clause 1, then $f$ is regularly homotopic to a self-transverse immersion with empty double point set, hence to an injective immersion, hence, since $M$ is closed, to an embedding ([[prop-a-proper-injective-immersion-is-a-smooth-embedding]]). In particular, if $X$ is simply connected and $m$ is even, then $f$ is regularly homotopic to an embedding whenever the oriented double point count of [[def-primary-double-point-obstruction-to-removing-self-intersections]] vanishes, so that the double points pair off by sign.

No claim is made that every self-transverse immersion is regularly homotopic to an embedding: the pairing and null-homotopy hypotheses are load-bearing, as the vanishing/knotting boundary remark below records.
consumer_patch.replace_proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses of the proposition, including Countable Choice, the chosen branch pairing with opposite signs, arcs avoiding every other double-point preimage, and a null-homotopic Whitney circle.

1.1 Choose disjoint source arc neighbourhoods $P,Q\subset M$, with smaller closed arc neighbourhoods inside them. Along either arc the immersion is an embedding because its interior contains no double-point preimage; shrink the source neighbourhoods using local embedding charts and compactness of the arcs. Their images meet each other only at the two prescribed corners, and meet no other branch there: otherwise a sequence of unwanted incidences as the neighbourhoods shrink would converge to an additional double-point preimage on an arc or to an extra branch at a prescribed double point. The two-branch condition at a double point is the exact actual supplier obligation. At the two corners use the complementary-sheet coordinates; opposite local signs allow the standard Whitney collar to be sewn between the arc collars. Its interior leaves the selected sheet in a transverse direction, and at a corner lies in the quadrant between the two sheet axes, so it meets neither axis. Compactness/properness excludes every remaining branch from a sufficiently small collar. As the circle is null-homotopic, the inner boundary of this collar also bounds a continuous disk (it is homotopic through the collar to the original circle). Attach that disk to the collar and smooth relative to a smaller collar using relative Whitney approximation, on the interior and with the fixed boundary model. Apply the immersion-image adapter to obtain an embedded disk $W$ with interior disjoint from all of $f(M)$, fixed on the collar and avoiding neighbourhoods of every other double point. [given, construct]

2.1 The branch-normal data along the Whitney circle give an admissible splitting into ranks $m-1$ and $m-1$ of the rank-$2m-2$ normal bundle of the collared disk. The orientations involved here are those over the contractible disk and the two source arc neighbourhoods; the original opposite-sign hypothesis is the corner compatibility. No orientation of all of $M$ or $X$ is added to clause 1. The corrected framing supplier asserts existence of an admissible extendible choice, permitting correction of the frame within one summand while fixing its subspace and its values at both corners. Its local surjection lemma proves that the inclusion $SO(m-1)\to SO(2m-2)$ is onto on $\pi_1$ for $m\ge3$, so one such correction kills the loop discrepancy from a global disk normal frame. The correction is supported in the interior of one boundary arc; it changes no sheet or disk. Obtain a clean framed disk. This uses an admissible extendible framing, never an arbitrary fixed circle-normal framing. [step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Choose the framing tube and the selected smaller source patch $P$ so that the local Whitney model isotopy $G_t$ is the identity near the image of $\partial P$, moves only the first sheet as compared with the fixed second sheet, and is supported in a compact tube around $W$. The model theorem provides an isotopy of the first sheet, relative to its boundary, whose final image intersects the fixed second sheet with precisely the prescribed cancelling pair removed. The tube is disjoint from all other source-image branches except the chosen sheet collars by step 1.1; shrink its radius using the compact disk core and the compact image of the source outside slightly enlarged $P,Q$, and use the fixed collar charts near the boundary. The local model is embedded on $P$ at every time and unchanged near $\partial P$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Define $f_t(x)=G_t(f(x))$ for $x\in P$, and $f_t(x)=f(x)$ for $x\notin P$. The two formulas agree on an open neighbourhood of $\partial P$ for every $t$, so they glue to a smooth map on $M\times I$. On $P$, $d f_t=dG_t\circ df$ is injective because $G_t$ is a local ambient diffeomorphism, and on the complement $df_t=df$ is injective; the agreement region handles patch boundaries. Thus every $f_t$ is an immersion and the family is a regular homotopy. The second source sheet $Q$ remains fixed. Applying $G_t$ to the entire immersion would preserve all coincidences and is explicitly not the construction. At the cancellation parameter the two branches may be tangent, although each source branch remains immersed. [step 3.1, construct]

5.1 At time one the model removes exactly the intersections at $r_1,r_2$ between the selected sheets and creates none. It creates no self-intersection within the moved patch because that patch stays embedded. A new intersection with any other branch is excluded by the tube cleanliness in step 3.1, and all other double-point neighbourhoods are fixed. Thus $\Sigma(f_1)=\Sigma(f)\setminus\{r_1,r_2\}$ and all remaining crossings retain their original self-transverse local models. The endpoint $f_1$ is self-transverse. Together with step 4.1 this proves clause 1 with the corrected endpoint-only transversality condition. [step 3.1, step 4.1]

6.1 There are finitely many double points: local injectivity excludes a neighbourhood of the diagonal in compact $M\times M$, and the transverse coincidence locus is a discrete closed subset of its compact complement. For a finite admissible pairing apply clause 1 successively. After each move the unmoved double-point germs and signs remain fixed. Transport the endpoints of any planned source arcs by the already constructed regular homotopy; the corresponding ambient Whitney circles remain null-homotopic because their parametrized loops vary by a homotopy. Rechoose the arcs by small source isotopies to avoid the finitely many remaining preimages and each other (two 1-dimensional arcs in $m\ge3$ can be made disjoint with endpoints fixed); this changes no ambient homotopy class. At every stage apply the adapter to the current immersion, rather than assume pairwise disjointness of all prior disks or closeness to an arbitrary null-homotopy preserves cleanliness. After finitely many removals the endpoint is an injective immersion of compact $M$, hence an embedding. Reparametrize each regular homotopy to be constant near its endpoints before concatenating, giving a smooth regular homotopy. [step 5.1, construct]

7.1 In the stated simply connected even-dimensional oriented-count situation, the vanishing finite sum of signs pairs each positive sign with a negative sign. Source connectedness and $m\ge3$ give disjoint embedded joining arcs avoiding every other double-point preimage; ambient simple connectivity makes every resulting Whitney circle null-homotopic. Thus the pairs are admissible and step 6.1 gives the claimed embedding endpoint. The orientation/count is used exactly where it is defined in the original clause, and no unconditional embedding claim is made. [given, step 6.1] ∎
consumer_patch.facts_surgery: Replace L2 by the exact immersion-image adapter and corrected admissible-framing supplier. L3 must say isotopy of the chosen first sheet with the second held fixed; it is not a common ambient action on the immersion. Retain original choice, sign, branch-label and orientation/count hypotheses.

supplier_surgical_corrections.replace_statement: Let $X^n$ be oriented and let $A^a,B^b\subset X$ be closed oriented complementary transverse embedded submanifolds with $a,b\ge3$ and $a+b=n$. Let $p,q$ have opposite local signs, and let $W$ be a clean collared Whitney disk for a Whitney circle joining them. The sheet data along its boundary admit an admissible framing of the rank-$n-2$ disk normal bundle that extends over $W$. An initially chosen admissible frame can be corrected within one of the rank-$a-1$ or rank-$b-1$ summands, supported away from the two corners, to make it extend. Thus a clean disk can be equipped with an admissible extendible framing. The assertion concerns existence after this allowed correction, and does not assert that every arbitrarily prescribed boundary normal frame extends. The rank-$n-1$ normal bundle of the boundary circle also contains the disk's inward tangent line and is not identified with the rank-$n-2$ disk normal bundle.
supplier_surgical_corrections.replace_proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses of the statement and a clean collared disk $W$.

1.1 Over the contractible disk the normal bundle has rank $n-2$ and a global orthonormal frame. Along the two boundary arcs the sheet tangencies give normal summands of ranks $a-1$ and $b-1$; compatible corner comparisons are the opposite-sign condition. Choose admissible frames of these summands along the intervals with the required common corner values. Existence of such choices is what the corrected compatible-framing supplier supplies; it supplies no preferred full-frame homotopy class. Compare the resulting total normal frame with the global disk frame. After matching orientations the discrepancy is a based loop in $SO(n-2)$. [given, construct]

1.2 Use the local normal-summand surjection lemma with $N=n-2$ and $r=a-1\ge2$ (or $r=b-1$). A loop in that summand realizes the inverse discrepancy. Multiplication by it, supported in the interior of one boundary arc, fixes the corner values, preserves the normal splitting and all tangency requirements, and kills the full-frame loop class. The corrected loop extends over the disk because it is nullhomotopic. Smooth the extension relative to the collar and apply Gram–Schmidt; the result is a smooth admissible normal trivialization and hence a framed Whitney tube. No boundary frame specified before correction is declared extendible. [step 1.1, construct] ∎

statement_surgery.remove: the data determine a preferred homotopy class of trivializations
statement_surgery.replace_with: the sheet data admit compatible boundary normal splittings and choices of admissible frames; the choices are permitted to vary within the sheet-normal summands and do not determine a preferred full-frame homotopy class

supplier_surgical_corrections.rank_correction: Separate the circle normal rank n-1 from the disk normal rank n-2 by its inward disk tangent line. Opposite signs give compatible corner data; they do not pick a full-frame homotopy class.

statement_surgery.remove: whose boundary restriction is the Whitney framing
statement_surgery.replace_with: whose rank-(n-2) boundary normal frame is an admissible choice compatible with the two sheet tangencies and corner data, allowing the correction inside a sheet-normal summand supplied by the framing lemma

supplier_surgical_corrections.required_note: If a specific admissible boundary framing is part of the input, framed means that actual framing extends; existence after regauging does not prove extension of that prescribed class.

statement_surgery.remove: the boundary values are the frames prescribed by the Whitney framing. Consequently the Whitney framing of $\gamma$ extends over $W$.
statement_surgery.replace_with: The first partial boundary frame can be extended while preserving its actual tangency conditions; the complementary partial frame is then chosen from its orthogonal complement. This produces an admissible extendible full frame, without preserving an arbitrary previously fixed complementary boundary frame.

supplier_surgical_corrections.tangency_correction: Along alpha, E is tangent to A; along beta, E is normal to B. Its complementary frame H is normal to A along alpha and tangent to B along beta. Do not state tangency to the wrong sheet or normality to a sheet absent at that arc. The rank of E is a-1 and that of H is b-1.
supplier_surgical_corrections.proof_obligation: Preserve connectivity clause (i), fixing its erroneous induction connectivity arithmetic if retained. The full fixed pair of boundary frames is an O(n-2) loop; extending the two Stiefel partial frames independently does not preserve their mutual orthogonality. Use actual Milnor construction or corrected framing lemma/surjection, never the old independent-extension claim.

statement_surgery.remove: its restriction to the sheet containing the arc $\alpha$ is the Whitney move of that sheet across $W$
statement_surgery.replace_with: its restriction to the sheet containing the arc $\alpha$, with the other sheet held fixed, is the Whitney move of that sheet across $W$

supplier_surgical_corrections.required_note: An auxiliary ambient isotopy moves the selected embedding relative to the fixed second embedding; applying it to both sheets preserves all intersections.

downstream_reconciliation: Recompute actual deps and linked citations on stable content after writers drain. In particular primary-double-point definition and double-point example have linked mentions omitted from draft deps; the example must not imply m=2 is covered by the m>=3 disjunction. The remark only needs endpoint transversality and regular homotopy, not all-times transversality. Framing supplier corrections also affect batch14 Whitney theorems and the bundle-triviality consumer of the frame-fields lemma; preserve clause (i) where that consumer uses it.
unresolved_actual_supplier_obligations: The actual definition/local-sheet supplier must exclude triple-point branches when it calls a point a two-sheet double point; self-transverse as a pairwise condition alone need not exclude triple points. Reconcile the stable batch19 definitions, do not invent an extra no-triple assumption in this patch.
The actual branch-arcs and label suppliers must support disjoint source arcs with compatible branch pairing and transported homotopy classes.

The actual local Whitney model/theorem must supply isotopy of one sheet relative its boundary with the other fixed; its global closed-submanifold phrasing cannot literally be applied to compact sheet patches without this explicit local proof interface.

The Stiefel-connectivity lemma exists as a draft file and was read; its stable proof and contract still require root reconciliation. The normal-summand adapter gives the exact remaining use rather than claiming a published acceptance.
Smooth relative approximation at a collared disk uses boundary-adapted extension; the fixed corner model is part of the Whitney-disk convention and must remain consistent across definition and model.
